# Issue #1154: One Shell-Argument Reading for the Whole Agentic Module

Issue [#1154](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1154) (E119):
Codex's shell tool `exec_command` sends the command under the argument key
`cmd`, while `progress.rs` read only `command`. The work-item read was never
recorded as attempted, and the stateless planner re-derived the identical
`gh issue view` call 78 times in a row (6.2M input tokens) until the client
compacted the thread. The full incident account, with the transcript excerpts,
is `docs/case-studies/issue-1154/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1154-1 | One shared `command_argument` for the whole `agentic_coding` module, reading the argument key from the client's declared tool schema (the key whose schema describes the shell command), falling back to `command`, `cmd`, `script`, and an array form joined for `shell`-style tools; the seven local copies are deleted. | Implemented: `rust/src/agentic_coding/tool_result.rs` gains the shared `command_argument` (string and joined-array forms) and `command_argument_key` (schema-driven key resolution for callers that hold the request's tool definitions); the seven former copies in `progress.rs`, `file_read.rs`, `tool_result.rs`, `narration.rs`, `command_reroute.rs`, `evidence_record.rs` and `workspace_change.rs` now delegate to it. |
| R1154-2 | Invariant independent of parsing: never plan a tool call whose name and arguments are byte-identical to one already attempted in the current turn window; if the planner would, report the stuck step and its last result instead of repeating it. | Implemented: `Progress::repeated_call` (`rust/src/agentic_coding/progress.rs`) recognizes a completed call by byte-identical arguments or the same canonical command/URL operand (the protocol layer may project `command` onto `cmd` before the transcript echoes the call), and `stop_repeated_call` (`rust/src/agentic_coding/planner.rs`) replaces the repeat with the `stuck_step_report` answer from `data/meta/work-item-steps.lino`. A completed call is the loop signature; a failed one keeps its existing bounded retry and the two-failure stop of issue #1133. |
| R1154-3 | After a successful read, the fetched text drives `plan_work_item_execution` exactly as on the Claude and Agent paths. | Implemented by the shared reading: `issue_view_url` now resolves under `cmd`, the read lands in `fetched_pages`, and `repository_work_item_objective` feeds `plan_work_item_execution` unchanged. Pinned by `codex_cmd_read_drives_execution_instead_of_repeating`. |
| R1154-4 | Tests: replay the Codex transcript's first two Responses items (`function_call` `exec_command {"cmd": …}` + `function_call_output`) through the Responses input conversion and assert the next plan is not another `gh issue view`; a table test over `{command}`, `{cmd}`, `{script}`, `{command:[…]}` yields the same recorded read. | Implemented in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1154_progress_arguments.rs`: the replay goes through `ResponsesRequest::to_chat_completion_request` (the server's own conversion), and the table covers all four spellings plus the twice-repeated transcript shape. |

# Issue #1155: Work-Item Read Validation and Honest Fallbacks

Issue [#1155](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1155) (E120):
an unauthenticated `gh issue view` printed its how-to-authenticate banner, the
Agent CLI echoed that output with the exit status dropped (`"metadata":
{"exit": 4}` in its own record, plain text in the tool message Formal AI
received), and the banner was accepted as the issue body. The run then wrote
`.formal-ai/general-change-plan.lino` and answered `planned_not_executed`
without ever trying the `webfetch` tool the client offered. The full account,
with the transcript excerpts, is `docs/case-studies/issue-1155/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1155-1 | The read observes its own status whatever the client sends: the planned read ends with `printf '\n__formal_ai_exit=%s\n' $?`, as data in `data/meta/work-item-steps.lino` (`issue_view_command`), and a non-zero status is a failed read. | Implemented: `issue_view_command` in `data/meta/work-item-steps.lino` (and the byte-identical embedded mirror) now appends the sentinel `printf`; `exit_sentinel` (`rust/src/agentic_coding/progress.rs`) reads the last `__formal_ai_exit=N` line and `work_item_read_failure_reason` turns any non-zero status into a failed read even when the client's echo carries no error flag. |
| R1155-2 | The read's shape is validated before it is accepted as the issue: a title line, a blank separator, then the body — output without that shape is a failed read, recorded with its text. | Implemented: `work_item_read_failure_reason` requires the `gh` reads to contain the blank-line separator (the incident banner has none) and the raw-body `curl` read to be non-empty text that does not begin like the API's JSON error blob; failed reads land in `Progress::failed_work_item_reads` with their reason and are never pushed to `fetched_pages`. Pinned by `a_status_less_gh_banner_is_a_failed_read_and_webfetch_of_the_issue_follows` and `a_failing_sentinel_outranks_a_well_shaped_output`. |
| R1155-3 | On a failed read, walk the fallbacks in order and record each attempt: the client's fetch tool on the issue URL, `curl -fsSL https://api.github.com/repos/<owner>/<repo>/<issues|pulls>/<n>`, `gh api`, then the prepared PR's title and body. | Implemented: `plan_work_item_read` (`rust/src/agentic_coding/general_execution.rs`) now plans, after the failed `gh` view: the fetch tool on the issue URL, `issue_rest_read_command` (credential-free `curl` with the raw-body `Accept` header), `issue_api_read_command` (two `gh api` calls printing title and body), and last `prepared_pull_reference` — the pull request the prompt names, fetched as page context. Pull-request work items read their REST `pulls/` endpoint. Every attempt is recorded; `Progress::work_item_read_attempts` lists them. Pinned by `the_rest_routes_follow_the_fetch_fallback_in_order`, `the_rest_fallback_of_a_pull_request_reads_the_pulls_endpoint`, `the_prepared_pull_request_is_the_last_read_fallback`. |
| R1155-4 | Only when all routes fail is `planned_not_executed` honest: the answer lists every read tried with its result, and the only write is never spent on the plan record when the goal could not be read. | Implemented: `work_item_read_failure_report` (filled from the `read_failed_report` data key) closes the run with every read, its reason and its first answer line — and `general_change_step` returns it before the `PLAN_PATH` write, so no plan record is written for an issue the session never read. Pinned by `an_exhausted_retrieval_reports_every_read_and_writes_no_plan_record`. |
| R1155-5 | Replay test from the transcript: with the Agent tool list (`webfetch`) and the `gh` result without exit status, the next plan is the `webfetch` of the issue URL; with the sentinel line `__formal_ai_exit=4` the read is a failure. | Implemented in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1155_read_validation.rs` (the file name the dispatch directed; the issue's Definition of Done names `issue_1155_work_item_read_failure.rs` — same tests, rename at registration if preferred): `a_status_less_gh_banner_is_a_failed_read_and_webfetch_of_the_issue_follows` replays the status-less echo, `with_the_sentinel_line_the_read_is_a_failure_and_the_fetch_follows` replays it with `__formal_ai_exit=4`, and both assert the next plan is the `webfetch` of the issue URL. |

Residuals for the main session: `REQUIREMENTS.md` and
`docs/requirements-traceability.md` regeneration
(`rust-script scripts/assemble-requirements.rs --write`), test registration in
`rust/tests/unit/mod.rs`, and the released-version manual confirmation row of
the issue's Definition of Done. Both ledger copies of
`data/meta/work-item-steps.lino` were edited byte-identically (the data/meta
tree is nominally main's; the issue requires the sentinel and the fallback
wording to live there as data).

## Issue #1156: Single output obligations

Source: https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1156

| Requirement | Drafted behavior | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Preserve the requested behavior in the agentic harness | Repeated identical quoted stdout requirements are deduplicated in first-mention order; distinct output operands retain their order. The generated output verifier therefore compares against the composed single obligation. Workflows use the recipe artifact stem rather than a shared run.yml path. | Drafted. Inline regressions cover duplicate and distinct output requirements. Existing output-verifier template already uses byte comparison and propagates process failure. No local execution was performed. Repository/task-specific workflow naming beyond artifact stems remains open. |

## Issue #1157: Idempotent recipe commits

Source: https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1157

| Requirement | Drafted behavior | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Preserve the requested behavior in the agentic harness | Recipe commits stage only declared artifacts and inspect the cached diff restricted to those paths. No-change runs emit __formal_ai_commit_unchanged, then still push and print the current hash. Continuations consume the planner evidence window, retaining already completed writes and commands. | Partial. Idempotent commit and continuation replay are drafted. Output ignore patterns and verification of artifacts after externally modified continuation state remain open. No local builds or tests were run. |

## Issue #1158: Pull request completion and feedback

Source: https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1158

| Requirement | Drafted behavior | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Preserve the requested behavior in the agentic harness | After a verified recipe commit, PR targets retrieve comments and reviews, update their description from artifact and verification commands, and mark draft PRs ready only with a clean working tree. Already-ready PRs are accepted. Nonempty comments, requested changes, or unreadable feedback block readiness with the observed feedback. | Partial. Feedback retrieval, description editing and guarded readiness are drafted. Deriving and applying arbitrary review-requested source edits remains open; feedback is never represented as resolved merely because it was fetched. |

## Issue #1159: Workspace prerequisite recovery

Source: https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1159

| Requirement | Drafted behavior | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Preserve the requested behavior in the agentic harness | Run failures are classified with the shared prerequisite classifier. Missing executables with FORMAL_AI_INSTALL_GRANT=workspace fetch their pinned publisher. A public process-free parser accepts only typed setup notation with a postcondition. Harness tools execute scoped setup, postcondition and one original-command retry, with explicit PATH and transcript binding; absolute/parent write scopes and shell/escalation setup programs are refused. | Partial. Typed publisher recovery is drafted and bounded. Ordinary publisher prose cannot become an executable recipe. Broader source discovery, per-process/network grants and typed recipes for publisher pages that lack them remain open. No local process installation, build or test was executed. |

## Issue #1160: Hive Mind prepared work continuation

| Requirement | Drafted behavior | Status |
|---|---|---|

## Issue #1161 Client Registry Names the Agent Config Env

Issue [#1161](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1161) (E126)
makes the client registry declare *how* a client is pointed at its config —
the env var that relocates it — instead of implying an `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`
relocation that also moves `gh`'s and git's config and breaks GitHub
authentication inside the session. The incident analysis, the per-client
evidence, and the fix live in `docs/case-studies/issue-1161/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1161-1 | Every `global_configs` entry in `data/seed/client-integrations.lino` can declare the environment variables that relocate its own config file (`config_env "VAR"` children), parsed into a new `ClientIntegrationGlobalConfig::config_env: Vec<String>`; entries whose file has no relocation variable declare an empty list. | Implemented: the `config_env` field and parser arm in `rust/src/seed/client_integrations.rs`, filled in `data/seed/client-integrations.lino` (and its committed `rust/embedded/` mirror) only where in-repo evidence exists. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1161_client_registry_env.rs`. |
| R1161-2 | `agent` names `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_CONFIG` (config file) and `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_CONFIG_DIR` (directory); `codex` and the `t3code` OpenAI-protocol entry name `CODEX_HOME`; `opencode`, `opencode-vscode` and `opencode-desktop` name `OPENCODE_CONFIG` and `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR`. | Implemented in the same seed file. Evidence per client: agent — the issue itself and the wrapper's own `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_CONFIG_CONTENT` one-shot mechanism; codex — `docs/configuration/output-sessions.md` (`$CODEX_HOME/sessions/…`), `experiments/agentic_cli_matrix/README.md` (`CODEX_HOME` → a directory holding `config.toml`) and `rust/tests/issue_760.rs`; t3code — its own ephemeral block relocates the same `config.toml` via `CODEX_HOME` (`docs/configuration/t3-code.md`); opencode family — each block's own ephemeral `config_env "OPENCODE_CONFIG"` / `config_dir_env "OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR"`. Pinned by the per-client assertions in the same test file. |
| R1161-3 | The declaration is a registry surface: `formal-ai clients --format json` carries it additively as `global_configs[].config_env` (plus the one-shot `config_env`/`config_dir_env`/`config_content_env`/`temp_home_env` top-level fields), and `formal-ai clients` prints it on each `global[...]` line. | Implemented in `rust/src/cli_clients.rs`. Additive only — the matrix (`experiments/agentic_cli_matrix/run_leg.sh`) still reads exactly the `verification.*` fields it read before. The projection is a bin module and is reviewed, not unit-tested; the underlying parsed data is what the test pins. |
| R1161-4 | A host integration contract is documented: a host that needs a task-local client config sets the declared variable and must not relocate `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` or `HOME` (the 2026-09-27 `gh`-auth incident, link-assistant/hive-mind#2314). | Implemented: the "Host integration contract" section and the *Relocate via* column in `docs/configuration/agentic-clis.md`, the registry-surface note in `docs/testing/agentic-cli-tools.md`. |
| R1161-5 | Clients whose global entry is a shell profile (`gemini`, `claude`, `qwen`, `aider`) or a fixed path with no evidenced variable (`cursor`, `grok`) declare none; no variable is fabricated. | Implemented and pinned by `entries_without_a_relocation_variable_declare_none` in the same test file. |
| R1161-6 | Hive Mind switches its Formal AI agent launcher from the `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` relocation to `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_CONFIG_DIR`/`LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_CONFIG`. | Cross-repo (link-assistant/hive-mind#2314): this repository's part — naming the variables as registry data and documenting the contract — is delivered here; the launcher change itself is tracked in the Hive Mind repository and is not confirmed from this repo. |
| R1161-7 | The declared relocation actually works end to end: the agent CLI is started with `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_CONFIG(_DIR)` pointing at a temporary config directory and serves the session from it (pull-request follow-up row: the smoke test half of the registry surface). | Open follow-up, cross-repo: the end-to-end smoke test needs the agent CLI's own repository to drive the launch; this repo pins the parsed declaration (`issue_1161_client_registry_env.rs`, including the embedded-mirror sync) and documents the contract (`docs/configuration/agentic-clis.md`), but no test here launches a client against a relocated config. |

## Issue #1165 Discovery on the Production Path

Issue [#1165](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1165) (E130)
puts the coding-by-discovery machinery on the path users and Hive Mind hit:
every stored program becomes a *cache entry* that names where a rediscovery
starts from, a cache miss routes to `research_coding_skill_gap` instead of a
template literal, and the whole cache is deletable by design. The analysis
and the wiring plan live in `docs/case-studies/issue-1165/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1165-1 | When the solver selects `SelectedRule::WriteProgram` and no cached procedure exists for the language/task, `research_coding_skill_gap` runs on the miss path and the answer is discovery-backed. | Module delivered: `rust/src/discovery_production.rs` provides `cached_or_research` (cache hit → row; miss → research, store, return), pinned offline by `miss_path_runs_research_and_stores_the_verified_procedure` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1165_discovery_production.rs`. Open wiring row: the call into the `WriteProgram` branch of `rust/src/solver.rs` is the integration step (this batch deliberately left `solver.rs` untouched for the wiring commit). |
| R1165-2 | `plan_work_item_execution` replaces a template-backed `execution_recipe` through the same miss path; `planned_not_executed` is never emitted for a recognised pair. | Same module: `cached_or_research` is the replacement entry point the executor calls. Open wiring row: the `general_execution.rs` call site lands with the solver wiring. |
| R1165-3 | A stored procedure is accepted only when its gap records a `rediscovery_query` and a `rediscovery_source`. | Implemented: `ProcedureCache::store` refuses rows without both fields (`store_rejects_procedure_without_rediscovery_fields`), and the policy seed `data/seed/program-cache-policy.lino` declares the requirement as data read by the module. |
| R1165-4 | `hello-world-programs.lino` and `ORACLE_SNAPSHOTS` are deleted; `knows_language` becomes "a grammar exists and discovery found a procedure". | Bootstrap conversion delivered: `rust/src/knowledge.rs` now gates every snapshot answer on `bootstrap_cache_active()`, which reads the policy seed — retiring the bootstrap is a seed edit, and `discovery_production::knows_language` implements the grammar-plus-procedure reading (kotlin answers, rust does not until its row exists). Open deletion rows: removing the seed file and the snapshot const themselves lands with the solver wiring (they touch the registry, `solver_handler_oracle.rs`, and ratchet tests outside this slice's file ownership). |
| R1165-5 | `entry`/`operation`/`ci_setup`/`documented_source` move from `stdout-program-contracts.lino` into the new cache format with a `rediscovery_query` per row. | Format delivered: `data/cache/coding-procedure-cache.lino` carries exactly those fields plus `rediscovery_query`/`rediscovery_source`/`content_id`; the reader/writer round-trip is pinned by `store_lookup_reload_roundtrip`. Open row: pruning the four fields from `stdout-program-contracts.lino` is a `data/meta` edit reserved for the wiring commit. |
| R1165-6 | No language row hard-codes a compile command once a verified procedure reproduces it. | Open row: `rust/src/coding/catalog/languages.rs` is owned by the meta-language slice (#1167) in this batch; the cache format can carry the reproduced check command (`verified_output`), and the deletion lands after the rediscovery run. |
| R1165-7 | A test deletes the entire cache and proves `research_coding_skill_gap` recreates rows with the same `content_id` for six languages including grammar-covered Pascal. | Offline half delivered: `delete_all_empties_the_cache_file` plus `content_id_is_fnv1a_of_entry_and_recomputed_on_store` (FNV-1a of the program bytes, recomputed on store, drift rejected on load). The six-language online run is `FORMAL_AI_LIVE_FETCH`-gated and lands with the solver wiring, where the live transport is constructed. |
| R1165-8 | The no-memorization gate fails on any verbatim per-language Hello World string in `data/`. | Open row: the gate lives in `rust/tests/unit/coding_discovery/no_memorization.rs`, shared test surface reserved for the wiring commit; the cache file itself carries no program rows until a verified run writes them. |
| R1165-9 | The discovery path serves the Hive Mind executor; the #1156 doubled output is bound once from the formalized requirement. | Delivered in the #1166 slice: `intent_formalization::formalize_request().unique_output_literal()` anchors the literal exactly once regardless of how many clauses mention it (`rust/tests/unit/issue_1166_obligation_routing.rs`). |
| R1165-10 | Three-roots parity: `procedure_cache` translated to JS/TS roots with cache hit/miss parity cases. | Open row: translation needs the `formal-ai translate` build; the module is written translation-shaped (pure functions, seed-driven policy, no crate-only types in the cache IO) for that step. |

## Issue #1166 The Request Formalized into Obligations

Issue [#1166](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1166) (E131)
replaces phrase matching with request formalization: an issue body parses
into an obligation graph whose nodes carry semantic kinds and anchored
literals, mentions of the same quoted literal collapse to one node (the
structural fix for the Kotlin doubled output of #1156), and nothing
underivable is silently discarded. The root-cause analysis lives in
`docs/case-studies/issue-1166/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1166-1 | An issue body parses into an `ObligationGraph`; every enumerated requirement produces an `ObligationNode` anchored to seed meanings/roles. | Implemented: `rust/src/intent_formalization/obligations.rs` (`formalize_request`) builds on `obligation_ledger::ObligationNode::build` — no new ledger type — and classifies clauses against `print_stdout`, `ci_workflow_request`, and the program-request roles. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1166_obligation_routing.rs`. |
| R1166-2 | Two or more mentions of the same quoted literal produce exactly one output-literal node. | Implemented: `coreference_pass` merges by literal value across clauses; `two_identical_output_clauses_produce_one_node` proves three mentions (intro, "print exactly", Expected Output) yield one node and one value. |
| R1166-3 | The executor derives its plan from obligation nodes and reports undischargeable nodes with byte spans. | Module delivered: the graph exposes `obligations_of_kind`, `gap_report` (node id + byte span + reason) for `gap_answer` consumers. Open wiring row: the `ci_workflow::requested_in` and `program_contract::explicit_stdout` call-site rewrites live in files owned by other slices of this batch; the terminal router's rewrite is delivered (see R1166-8). |
| R1166-4 | A completed run emits an obligation report for each undischargeable node; none is silently omitted. | Delivered at module level: `ObligationGraph::gap_report` and `underivable()`; the executor emission is the same wiring row as R1166-3. |
| R1166-5 | An underivable clause yields `ObligationExpectation::Underivable`, split or reported, never discarded. | Implemented and pinned: `unknown_requirement_clause_yields_underivable_node_not_panic` (the ledger's own expectation semantics; the classifier leaves such nodes unclassified). |
| R1166-6 | A translated body (en/ru/hi/zh/es) yields the same graph modulo the language tag. | Implemented for the fixture family: `kotlin_issue_ru_yields_same_obligation_count_as_en` and `kotlin_issue_hi_zh_es_yield_same_graph_modulo_language_tag` over `rust/tests/fixtures/issue-1166/hello-world-kotlin-{en,ru,hi,zh,es}.txt`; classification reads the seed lexicon's multilingual lexemes with documented per-language fallback tables for the style/naming/badge vocabulary the seeds do not own yet. |
| R1166-7 | A paraphrased body produces an equivalent graph. | Implemented: `paraphrase_en_yields_same_obligation_count_as_canonical_en` over `hello-world-kotlin-paraphrase-en.txt`. |
| R1166-8 | Routing decides by the formalized request, not the leading word. | Implemented for the terminal router: `leading_shell_command` in `rust/src/solver_terminal.rs` now consults `request_carries_work_obligations` — a quoted output literal plus an authoring clause (program, CI, style, naming, badge) is a sentence about building something, in any of the five languages, while `git status` and `echo "Hello, World!"` stay commands (`work_obligation_requests_are_not_terminal_commands`). |

## Issue #1168 Generated Code Uses Versions Resolved at Generation Time

Issue [#1168](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1168) (E133)
makes every third-party version a generated artifact pins — action refs,
toolchain versions, the Java LTS — a *resolved* value with provenance, never a
memorized string. Resolution happens at generation time from the publisher's
own API, is recorded in the derivation, and degrades loudly (cache, then
shipped baseline, each said out loud) rather than silently going stale.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1168-1 | The latest release tag and its commit SHA for every third-party GitHub Action in a generated CI workflow are fetched from `https://api.github.com/repos/{publisher}/{repo}/releases/latest` (then `commits/{tag}` for the SHA). | Implemented: `resolve_github` in `rust/src/version_resolution.rs`, covering `actions/checkout`, `actions/setup-java`, `fwilhe2/setup-kotlin`, `actions/setup-python`; pinned by mocked-transport tests (`resolves_every_pin_from_live_fixtures`). |
| R1168-2 | The Kotlin version is the latest `JetBrains/kotlin` release tag. | Implemented in the same module (`v2.4.20` as shipped baseline); the tag feeds `fwilhe2/setup-kotlin`'s `version:` argument through `fill_workflow_versions`. |
| R1168-3 | The Java version is Adoptium's own `most_recent_lts`, never a literal `'21'`. | Implemented: `resolve_java_lts` reads `https://api.adoptium.net/v3/info/available_releases` (25 as shipped baseline). |
| R1168-4 | Every resolved version is recorded in the derivation as a `SourceCapture` (source_url, fetched_at, sha256, cached, bytes) via the existing `CachedSourceClient`. | Implemented: `VersionSet::record` appends each capture's provenance plus one `version_resolution` line per pin; pinned by `records_the_resolution_in_the_derivation`. |
| R1168-5 | When the live API is unreachable, the most recent cached capture is used and the answer is annotated `(version resolved from cache; fetched_at=<timestamp>)`. | Implemented: `CachedSourceClient` replay supplies `Origin::Cache`, and `provenance_note` emits exactly that wording — extended to the shipped baseline, which annotates `(version resolved from the shipped baseline measured <date>)`; `ci_workflow::render` prepends the notes as workflow comments. Pinned by `offline_replays_the_cached_capture_and_says_so`. |
| R1168-6 | `workflow_template` and `ci_setup` values carry placeholders, never literal SHAs or bare versions. | Code half implemented: `fill_workflow_versions` fills `{checkout_ref}` … `{java_lts}` **and** still rewrites any stale `@<sha>` / `version: '…'` literal that slips through, scoped per action block. The two `data/meta` template files themselves (and their embedded mirrors) are rewired by the integrating commit; until then the R1168-8 gate is red exactly there. |
| R1168-7 | A CI gate fails on any `@<sha>` or bare version literal for a third-party action or toolchain in `data/`. | Implemented: `scripts/check-generated-version-literals.rs` (scans `data/` minus `data/cache/`; the toolchains baseline is exempt by shape, not by name), with embedded tests plus `rust/tests/unit/issue_1168_latest_versions.rs` pinning that findings are confined to the two templates awaiting the R6 rewrite. CI-stage wiring rides with the R6 rewrite in the integrating commit. |
| R1168-8 | Three-roots parity: `version_resolution.rs` translated to js/ts and parity cases added. | Open follow-up: the `formal-ai translate` pass and the `data/parity/cross-runtime-synthesis.json` cases need a build to generate and verify; the Rust contract is pinned here so the translation has a fixed target. |

The shipped baseline in `data/seed/toolchains.lino` (`generated_version` records)
was measured 2026-09-30 against the live APIs and tags: checkout `v7.0.1`
(`3d3c42e5…`), setup-java `v6.0.1` (`de7274f0…`), setup-kotlin `v2.0`

## Issue #1169 Every Dependency at Its Latest Release

Issue [#1169](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1169) (E134)
makes dependency currency a fact the repository enforces, not a habit it
hopes for: every dependency — crates, npm packages, GitHub Action refs, the
container base image, the rustc floor — sits at its publisher's latest
release, and a gate fails when one does not. The one sanctioned hold-back is
an in-tree annotation naming the issue that tracks it.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1169-1 | A gate reads every ecosystem the repository declares: `rust/Cargo.toml` against `rust/Cargo.lock`, every `package.json` against its lockfile (manifest-range fallback where a directory ships no lock), `uses:` refs in `.github/workflows` and composite actions, `FROM` bases in the `Dockerfile`, and the `rust-version` floor. | Implemented: `collect` in `scripts/check-dependencies-latest.rs`, walking with `node_modules`/`target`/`.git`/`.claude`/`cache` excluded; pinned by `the_repository_tree_collects_every_ecosystem` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1169_dependency_currency.rs`. |
| R1169-2 | "Latest" comes from the publisher's own registry — crates.io `max_stable_version`, npm `dist-tags.latest`, GitHub `releases/latest`, Docker Hub tags, the rust stable channel — never a memorized list. | Implemented: the `latest_*` fetchers (curl + `USER_AGENT`, 30 s cap), each parsed from the publisher's own answer. |
| R1169-3 | A dependency may be held back only with a same-line annotation naming the tracking issue; the gate verifies the annotation, and drift without one fails. | Implemented: `blocked_annotation` requires `# blocked: <https://…/issues/…>` in Cargo.toml and a `"<name>//"` sibling key in package.json; blocked findings are reported with `(blocked)` and do not fail, unblocked drift exits 1. Documented in `CONTRIBUTING.md` beside the self-maintained-dependencies policy. `links-notation = "0.16.1" # blocked: …` is the first resident: lino-objects-codec 0.7.0 requires `^0.16`. |
| R1169-4 | The tree itself is moved to latest: `cargo update` resolution (already applied to `rust/Cargo.lock` — command-stream 1.2.0, webrtc 0.21.0, toml_edit 0.25.15, clap 4.6.7 …), npm manifests hand-bumped with real registry integrity (react/react-dom 19.3.0, dompurify 3.4.16, marked 18.0.14, command-stream 1.2.0, electron 44.4.5, electron-builder 26.17.0 with its app-builder-lib/dmg-builder/builder-util/electron-publish/squirrel-windows ring, playwright 1.63.0 across desktop + e2e + vscode), and the pin edits (`konrad/box-dind` 2.10.2, `actions/cache` v6 in both composite actions, `zizmor-action` v0.6.4). | Applied in this commit; the desktop/e2e lock edits were verified closed by a before/after range-resolution diff over the `packages` map (only the intended entries changed; nested `@noble/hashes` 1.8.0 added for app-builder-lib 26.17.0's narrowed range). |
| R1169-5 | A daily job refreshes the registry answers, applies every unblocked bump, re-resolves lockfiles, re-runs the CI gates, and opens one PR with whatever moved. | Implemented: `.github/workflows/dependencies-latest.yml` (cron `23 5 * * *`, off the fleet's :00 stampede per issue #1021) — `--refresh-snapshot`, `--apply --offline`, `cargo update --workspace`, `bun install` per manifest directory, `run-ci-gates` all three stages, `peter-evans/create-pull-request@v8`. Not yet run (needs CI). |
| R1169-6 | Registry flakiness never reddens CI: `--offline` answers from `data/meta/dependency-registry-snapshot.lino`, written by `--refresh-snapshot`; an unreachable registry exits 3, distinct from findings. | Implemented: `read_snapshot`/`write_snapshot` (flat lino, one `registry_entry <ecosystem>/<name>` record per answer) and the exit-code ladder 0/1/2/3 in `main`. |
| R1169-7 | `--apply` moves manifests (not lockfiles) and leaves annotated pins alone; lockfiles are re-derived by the daily job's resolvers. | Implemented: `apply_latest` + the per-ecosystem line rewriters; pinned by `apply_moves_unblocked_manifests_and_leaves_blocked_alone`. |
| R1169-8 | The gate's parsers and rules are pinned by tests that compile the script into the unit suite. | Implemented: eleven embedded tests in the script plus three fixture-tree tests in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1169_dependency_currency.rs` (`#[path]` include, the `ci_gates.rs` idiom). |

Residuals for the integrating commit: the unit-suite registration line in
`rust/tests/unit/mod.rs` (shared wiring, deliberately untouched here), the
`data/meta/ci-gates/` registration shard, and the first
`--refresh-snapshot` run to seed `data/meta/dependency-registry-snapshot.lino`
(all under the parent's `data/meta`/shared-wiring ownership). The gate is
expected to run red on first CI invocation for legacy pins it newly
surfaces — most `uses:` refs across `.github/workflows` predate this gate
and carry no blocked annotation; the daily job's first PR is the designed
way they move.

VS Code packaging residual: `@vscode/vsce` remains at `^3.9.2`, matching
`vscode/package-lock.json`. This is an unresolved dependency currency gap. Publisher
metadata for 4.0.0 requires Node >=22 and a changed dependency graph, including
`@napi-rs/keyring`, `@vscode/vsce-sign` ^2.1.0, and Secretlint core/types/source
creator packages. Complete this bump in CI with a full npm lockfile resolution;
replacing the top-level package version alone would leave missing dependencies.
Playwright and playwright-core are updated together to 1.63.0 in that lockfile,
using the same registry integrity records as the e2e lockfile. No builds or tests
were run for these integration changes.

## Issue #1172 Factual QA Subject-Verified Lookup

Issue [#1172](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1172) (E137,
part of the #1183 umbrella) reports that "What is the capital of Australia?"
was answered with "The capital of the United States is Washington, D.C." —
the alias "us" matched as a raw substring inside "a**us**tralia". A wrong
answer is worse than no answer. This shard pins the delivered word-boundary
fix (R1, R4, R10, R11 of the issue) and records the open follow-ups (R2, R3,
R5–R9, and the parity-corpus half of R10 as R1172-12) honestly. The root-cause
analysis, the corrected issue-0127 rows, and
the evidence live in `docs/case-studies/issue-1172/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1172-1 | A subject alias or question keyword may match the normalized prompt only at word boundaries (tokenized comparison), never as a raw substring inside a longer word: "us" must not match inside "australia"; multi-word aliases ("united states") match as consecutive token sequences; CJK surfaces, which have no inter-word spaces, keep substring matching. | Implemented: `FactRecord::matches_normalized` (`rust/src/seed/facts.rs`) now gates every alias and keyword through the new associated `FactRecord::contains_word_sequence`, which tokenizes the phrase with the same `engine::normalize_prompt` the caller applied to the prompt and requires a consecutive token run — the same contract as `seed::meanings::surface_present` (issue #386), mirrored for the fact store's own matching path. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1172_factual_qa_subject_match.rs`. |
| R1172-2 | A fact record may answer only when the formalized question's subject (Wikidata Q-id) equals the record's `subject_qid`; alias/keyword matching is retired as the primary mechanism. | Open follow-up: requires the question formalizer's subject anchors (`formalize_prompt_candidates`) as the selection gate. R1172-1's word-boundary matcher removes the measured false-hit class in the meantime and remains the surface hint R2 keeps as a last resort. |
| R1172-3 | When no seeded fact's subject matches, the engine queries Wikidata live for the requested property and answers from the returned statement with its reference URL. | Open follow-up for the Rust engine (the live fetch-and-formalize pipeline is #1163/E128's delivery). The browser worker's `resolveFactQueryViaWikidata` (`js/worker/formal_ai_worker_10.js`) already exists and, with R1172-4, is now actually reached for unseeded subjects: the substring false-hit used to mask the cache miss. |
| R1172-4 | `fact_store_resolves` returns `false` for a prompt whose subject has no seeded record, so the open-web/live-query planner (issue #989) is not blocked by a false hit. | Implemented: `fact_store_resolves` (`rust/src/solver_handlers/benchmark_prompts.rs`) delegates to the corrected matcher, so "What is the capital of Australia?" resolves to `false` and the planner may release the prompt to the open web instead of discarding the wrong cached answer (issue #1138's regression is not reintroduced: seeded subjects still resolve `true`). Pinned by `usa_fact_no_longer_answers_australia_prompts` and `engine_no_longer_answers_australia_with_washington` in the same test file. |
| R1172-5 | Definitions ("What does X mean?") resolve via Wiktionary or Wikidata lexemes, never the canned web-search paragraph. | Shared root cause with #1173 (E138): the canned paragraph is deleted by that issue's lane in this pull request; the Wiktionary/lexeme resolution itself remains open there. |
| R1172-6 | Comparisons ("Compare X and Y") answer with both subjects' aligned properties and the stated differences. | Open follow-up. |
| R1172-7 | Questions over prompt-supplied text are answered purely from the formalized text's own statements, with zero network calls. | Open follow-up; its routing precondition ("text is given in the prompt" is `locus prompt`) is owned by the #1175 (E140) lane of this pull request. |
| R1172-8 | Explanations retrieve pages, formalize them, and answer from the statements that define the concept, each claim citing its source. | Open follow-up; depends on #1163 (E128) for the retrieve-and-formalize path. |
| R1172-9 | Seeded `facts.lino` entries the live path can reproduce are deleted in favor of fetched-and-cached records. | Open follow-up; blocked on R1172-2/R1172-3 landing first (there is no live path to cache from yet in the Rust engine). |
| R1172-10 | The fix lands in every root that has the defect: Rust, JavaScript, and TypeScript if a twin exists. | Implemented in every root: Rust (`rust/src/seed/facts.rs`, `detect_subject_alias` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/benchmark_prompts.rs`), JavaScript (`tryFactLookup`, `tryCoreferenceFactLookup`, `matchingAntecedentFactAlias`) and the TypeScript twin regenerated from it by `scripts/translate-es.mjs`. The same probes are pinned in both roots: `rust/tests/unit/issue_1172_factual_qa_subject_match.rs` and `rust/tests/web/issue-1172-1173-worker-parity.test.mjs` (Australia is not answered as the United States; "USA" still is). |
| R1172-11 | `docs/requirements/issue-0127-structured-fact-query-reasoning-requirements.md` rows R173, R174, R177 no longer stand as "Implemented" while contradicted by the Australia measurement; the substring defect and its correction are cited in each row. | Implemented: all three rows now record the substring defect and its word-boundary correction with issue #1172 cited (see the shard). |
| R1172-12 | The word-boundary matcher's Rust and JavaScript spellings stay provably equivalent through a shared cross-runtime parity case (pull-request follow-up row: the parity corpus half of R1172-10). | Open follow-up: `data/parity/cross-runtime-synthesis.json` gained no case for the fact-matching word-boundary contract; the worker-parity lane of this pull request did not land, so the equivalence of `contains_word_sequence` and `surfacePresent` is pinned only by their parallel unit tests, not by a parity corpus row. |

## Issue #1173 No Canned Search Answer in the Unknown-Reasoning Fallback

Issue [#1173](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1173) (E138)
deletes the descriptive "Web search requested for `…`" paragraph as an answer
surface and makes the unknown-reasoning fallback execute its web search. The
source analysis, the deleted answer arms, and the evidence live in
`docs/case-studies/issue-1173/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1173-1 | The unknown-reasoning fallback runs the executed search for its focus and answers from the captured statements with citations; offline it answers with the existing `web_search_unavailable` response plus what the offline cache holds. | Implemented: the fallback arm in `rust/src/solver_unknown_reasoning.rs` hands its focus to `answer_web_search_query`, which now executes through `execute_web_search_answer` (`rust/src/solver_handlers/web_requests/live_search.rs`) against the process source cache. Captured sources answer via issue #709 statement fusion with per-statement citations; an offline or cache-miss run still reads the cache and then degrades to the localized `web_search_unavailable` response naming the focus. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1173_fallback_executes_search.rs`. |
| R1173-2 | `answer_web_search_query`'s descriptive text is no longer an answer anywhere; it survives only as narration of the planned search (or is deleted). | Implemented by deletion: every `format!` arm of the old paragraph (default, latest-news, open-research; en and ru) is removed from `rust/src/solver_handlers/web_requests.rs`, and `try_web_search` delegates to the executed path. The provider list and fusion formula survive only as log events (`web_search:provider_planned`, `web_search:fusion_planned`) on the unavailable path — narration in the reasoning trace, never the answer. Pinned by the `no_canned_description` assertions across the same test file. |
| R1173-3 | A request that does not need outside knowledge never reaches the fallback: each class gets its handler through #1175 (routing) and the class issues (#1172, #1174, #1176, #1177, #1178, #1186). | Owned by the #1175 routing work delivered alongside this shard in the same pull request; see its requirement shard. This shard fixes what the fallback does for the prompts that remain. |
| R1173-4 | The answer states what was searched, which pages were read (URL + hash, through #1184's derivation), and which statements the answer rests on. | Implemented for the executed body: the localized fusion header names the query, and every statement lists its source URLs and quotes (issue #709 `render_markdown`). Page-content hashes are #1184's derivation and are not claimed here. Pinned by the citation assertions in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1173_fallback_executes_search.rs`. |
| R1173-5 | Three-roots parity: the browser worker's fallback follows the same rule (translated code, parity case). | Implemented 2026-10-07: the browser worker applies the same rule — `guardCannedWebSearchAnswer` (`js/worker/formal_ai_worker_reasoning_guards.js`) turns any canned search-machinery description into the seeded `web_search_unavailable` response naming the query, and an offline research prompt never shows it; pinned by `rust/tests/web/issue-1172-1173-worker-parity.test.mjs`. The TypeScript twin is regenerated from the worker. |

## Issue #1174 Text Transforms Answered Formally

Issue [#1174](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1174) (E139,
part of the #1183 umbrella) gives the solver the text-transform family —
free-text summarization, register rewriting, grammar correction, genre
writing (Conventional Commits and business email), and sentence-level
translation — as computations over text the request itself carries, with all
recognition vocabulary and response prose in seed data and every honest
boundary (nothing to change, slot missing, word unknown) reported through a
seeded template instead of a guess. The probes, the before/after evidence,
and the honest boundaries live in `docs/case-studies/issue-1174/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1174-1 | A summarization request that carries its own paragraph ("Summarize this paragraph: …") is answered with a weight-ranked selection of its statements under a ~30% bound (at least two, always at least one short of the input), never an echo of the source; a request that names no text is declined so the seeded-topic handlers keep it. | Delivered: `handle_summarization_request` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/summarization_request.rs` recognizes the act through the `text_summarization_action` role (surfaces in `data/seed/meanings-summarization.lino`, five languages), extracts the payload with `free_text_payload`, and runs the shared formalize → summarize → deformalize pipeline (`crate::summarization`); statements under two are declined, and the selection bound can never equal the input length. |
| R1174-2 | A register-rewriting request ("Rewrite this formally: can u send me the report asap thx") substitutes every seeded informal token with its formal equivalent (casing kept), splices seeded politeness phrase rules, logs each substitution, and returns a body with no informal token; an already-formal text passes through unchanged with an honest note. | Delivered: `handle_rewrite_register` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/text_rewrite.rs` reads word pairs and phrase rules from `data/seed/register-lexicon.lino` (English and Russian), keeps source casing via `rebuild_core`, and answers through the `text_transform_register` response family; the no-change branch renders `text_transform_rewrite_unchanged`. |
| R1174-3 | A grammar-correction request ("Correct the grammar: She don't like apples and he have two cat.") re-agrees adjacent third-person subject + verb pairs and pluralizes a numeral's noun (irregular plurals and uncountables respected), logging each fix with the rule that fired; a clean text is reported as already grammatical. | Delivered: `handle_grammar_correction` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/text_rewrite.rs` applies the `subject_verb_rule`, `numeral_noun_rule`, `plural_exception` and `uncountable_noun` records of `data/seed/agreement-rules.lino` token by token; corrections render line by line through `text_transform_grammar_line` with the rule name, the body through `text_transform_grammar_result`, and the clean case through `text_transform_grammar_clean`. |
| R1174-4 | A commit-message request ("Write a commit message: correct an off-by-one error in the pagination helper") composes a Conventional Commits line from the described change — verb mapped to the seeded type, scope after the seeded preposition, effect between — and names the genre's missing slots through the incomplete template instead of fabricating them. | Delivered: the `commit_message` arm of `handle_genre_writing` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/text_rewrite.rs` fills the `{type}({component}): {imperative} {effect}` and no-scope templates of `data/seed/writing-genre-styleguides.lino` (styleguide URL logged); a request missing the verb or effect answers through `text_transform_genre_incomplete` at reduced confidence. |
| R1174-5 | An email request ("Write an email to my team: I am taking a day off on Friday because I am tired.") composes the seeded part frames — greeting with recipient, intent, reason after the seeded cue, weekday date, closing — in the styleguide's declared order. | Delivered: the `email` arm of `handle_genre_writing` reads the part sequence, frames, recipient preposition, possessives and reason cue from `data/seed/writing-genre-styleguides.lino`, resolves the weekday through the `calendar_weekday` role, and renders optional parts (reason, date) only when their cues are present. |
| R1174-6 | A translation request whose text has no quotes or backticks ("Translate to Russian: The weather is nice today, let's go for a walk.") still translates: the free sentence after the command head goes word by word through the pipeline, function words are dropped and logged, resolved words carry their meaning ids, unknown words are named through the seeded template rather than hidden, and a sentence with nothing translatable reports the honest gap. | Delivered: `translate_free_sentence` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/mod.rs` (reached from `try_translation` when no quotable surface exists and source ≠ target) calls `TranslationPipeline::translate_sentence` (`rust/src/translation/pipeline.rs`), which resolves each token against seeded compositional lemmas and the cache before any network request, keeps the source token order, and preserves terminal punctuation; unknown words append the `text_transform_translation_unknown` note. |
| R1174-7 | The whole family is a pure function of seed data — cues, pairs, rules, frames, and response prose live in `data/seed/` with five-language response parity — every new token the seed files introduce resolves under the total-closure audit, and no hardcoded-language or literal-predicate debt is added. | Delivered: recognition vocabulary in `register-lexicon.lino`, `agreement-rules.lino`, `writing-genre-styleguides.lino`, `meanings-summarization.lino`; responses in `multilingual-responses-text-transform.lino` (en/ru/hi/zh/es); the new intent keys and identifiers grounded by five-field definitions in `meanings-text-transform.lino` (registered in `data/meta/seed-registry.lino`); all six files measured net-zero unresolved under `scripts/audit-total-closure.py`, and the literal-predicate count stays at its 536 ceiling. |
| R1174-8 | The family is covered by automated tests pinning each probe's intent and computed body, including the honest boundaries (no text to summarize, already formal, already grammatical, missing slots, declined prompts). | Delivered: `rust/tests/unit/issue_1174_text_transform.rs` exercises the handlers directly (the dispatch wiring belongs to the #1175 routing work delivered in the same pull request); its registration in `rust/tests/unit/mod.rs` and the dispatch entries are owned by the coordinating session. |
| R1174-9 | Every answer for these five classes carries its derivation as links (formalized statements, the source-language surface, the target grammar rule or style-guide clause applied) inspectable via `formal-ai explain <answer>`, per the umbrella's white-box requirement (#1183 acceptance item 2). | Open follow-up (issue R7): the handlers log their derivations as evidence-log events (`register_rewrite` per substitution, `grammar_correction` per fix with its rule, `genre_styleguide`/`genre_composition`, and the summarization/translation events), so the reasoning is inspectable in the dialog log today; the `formal-ai explain <answer>` surface over those links is not delivered and remains open. |

## Issue #1175 Routing by Formalization, Not by a Surface Word

Issue [#1175](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1175) (E140,
part of the #1183 umbrella) stops two intent detectors from claiming a prompt
because a single word matched a recognition surface: the terminal-command
detector fired whenever a prompt's first word was a seed shell token, and the
software-project detector picked its artifact kind from an artifact surface
anywhere in the prompt. The source analysis, the before/after evidence, and
the honest boundaries live in `docs/case-studies/issue-1175/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1175-1 | The leading-token path of terminal-command detection claims a prompt only when the words after the leading shell token parse as command arguments: no question mark (ASCII or full-width), no colon followed by a space outside quotes, no bare token ending in sentence punctuation (except a token that is entirely dots — `.` and `..` are paths), and no bare function word from a small closed marker list; quoted spans are masked before every check, so prose inside quotes is data. Command shapes stay accepted, including `find . -name '*.log' -size +10M`, `make test`, `head -n 5 main.rs`, `export FOO=bar`, `touch newfile.txt`, `git commit -m 'fix the parser bug'`, and single bare tokens; the backtick+verb and verb+phrase trigger paths are unchanged. | Implemented in `rust/src/solver_terminal.rs` (`parses_as_command_arguments` with `mask_quoted_spans` and `NATURAL_LANGUAGE_MARKER_WORDS`, gated into `leading_shell_command`); JavaScript twin in `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_09.js` (`parsesAsCommandArguments` with `maskQuotedSpans`). Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1175_routing.rs`. |
| R1175-2 | The software-project handler selects its artifact kind only from the head noun of the object phrase governed by the authoring verb — the first boundary-delimited segment after the verb (benefactives and determiners skipped), or, for a verb-final (subject-object-verb) request with nothing after the verb, the last segment before it — never from an artifact word elsewhere in the prompt. Artifact-headed requests keep the frame in every lexicalised language, including unspaced CJK. | Implemented in `rust/src/solver_handlers/software_project.rs` (`object_phrase_artifact` with `skip_object_phrase_lead`, `object_phrase_segments`, `boundary_cut`, `match_artifact_head`, `scan_action_from`; the old any-position `match_artifact`/`scan_match` are deleted; `software_project_claims` and `from_prompt` both route through the new analysis). Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1175_routing.rs`. |
| R1175-3 | Routing is decided by a full capability-table refactor so no handler can claim on a surface match alone. | Partial: this change delivers the targeted guards at the two reported detection sites and pins them with held-out probes; the wholesale capability-table refactor of every handler's claims is not delivered here and remains open. |
| R1175-4 | A 200-prompt CI routing probe set covers every intent lane with a coverage budget, so a misroute of this class cannot land unnoticed. | Partial: 24 held-out routing probes (en, ru, hi, zh — including the three reported prompts, five prose-starting-with-a-shell-word prompts, seven command shapes, and five incidental-artifact prompts) are delivered in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1175_routing.rs`, each verified absent from `data/seed/`; the 200-prompt set with per-intent coverage budgeting is not. |
| R1175-5 | Three-roots parity: the browser worker's terminal detection and software-project detection follow the same rules. | Implemented 2026-10-07: the terminal-detection guard is mirrored in `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_09.js`, and the software-project guard in `detectSoftwareObjectPhrase` (`js/worker/formal_ai_worker_11.js`, over the shared `objectPhraseArtifact`), so the browser reads the artifact from the request's object phrase as Rust does; `ts/` is regenerated from both. Pinned by `rust/tests/web/issue-1175-software-object-phrase.test.mjs`. |

## Issue #1176 Quantities, Dates and Statistics Computed Exactly

Issue [#1176](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1176) (E141,
part of the #1183 umbrella) replaces four classes of canned or wrong answers —
calendar offsets, statistics over stated lists, unit conversion, and
price×count word problems — with exact local computation that shows its
arithmetic. The probes, the before/after evidence, and the honest boundaries
live in `docs/case-studies/issue-1176/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1176-1 | Quantities are formalized with value and unit, the unit resolved to a Wikidata item with its conversion factor, and conversions are exact decimal arithmetic; "26.2 miles in km" → 42.1648128 km with the factor 1.609344 cited. | Partial: `rust/src/solver_handlers/unit_conversion.rs` computes conversions on an exact `mantissa × 10⁻ˢᶜᵃˡᵉ` decimal (26.2 × 1.609344 = 42.1648128, 10 km → ≈6.2137119 miles, °C→°F as the formula 25 × 9/5 + 32 = 77) and the answer cites the factor it used. Factors, formulas and unit surfaces are seed data in `data/seed/meanings-units.lino`, each unit grounded in its Wikidata item (mile Q253276, inch Q218593, …) — a hand-grounded starter table, not live P2370 reads; units are resolved by lexicon surface, not by full item resolution. Unknown units (furlongs) and ambiguous lists ("5 feet 9 inches in cm") are declined. |
| R1176-2 | Word problems are formalized into quantities and relations (price × count, payment − cost) and solved, with the derivation shown (pens: 20 − 4 × 3 = 8). | Partial: `handle_word_problem` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/statistics.rs` answers the unit-price pattern — "at N dollars each" plus a count (and a payment for the change variant) — as exact decimal arithmetic with the derivation in the answer body (change: 20 − 4 × 3 = 8; total: 4 × 3 = 12), the markers being seed vocabulary in every supported language. Only this pattern is recognised; general relation extraction through the equation solver is not delivered. |
| R1176-3 | Descriptive statistics (mean, median, mode, variance, standard deviation, percentile, range) are meanings with formulas in `data/seed/meanings-statistics.lino`, applied to the extracted list; mean(4, 8, 15, 16, 23, 42) = 18, median = 15.5. | Partial: all six seed-defined operations except percentile are implemented in `rust/src/solver_handlers/statistics.rs` — each a meaning with formula and source URL in `data/seed/meanings-statistics.lino`, labels localised from the seed lexemes. Mean 108 / 6 = 18 and median (15 + 16) / 2 = 15.5 are exact; the variance is the exact fraction 5460/36 rendered to seven digits with an explicit ≈ marker (the standard deviation is the one marked approximation). Percentile is not delivered. |
| R1176-4 | Calendar arithmetic reads the formalized offset (quantity and unit: days, weeks, months) and computes modulo the cycle: 100 days after Monday = 14 weeks + 2 days → Wednesday. | Partial: `try_calendar_reasoning` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/calendar.rs` now reads the stated offset — numeral plus unit surface from the seed (`calendar_day`, `calendar_week`), spelled cardinals included, CJK-unspaced "100天" included — and shifts by it: 100 days after Monday is Wednesday with the derivation "100 days = 14 weeks + 2 days"; whole weeks state that the weekday is unchanged. A bare "the day after X" keeps its original ±1 reading. Month offsets and real-calendar date arithmetic (month lengths, leap years) are not delivered; weekday-cycle arithmetic only. |
| R1176-5 | Each answer carries its derivation and all three roots answer identically. | Implemented 2026-10-07: every answer body shows the arithmetic it performed (derivation strings in `data/seed/multilingual-responses-quantities.lino`, 12 intents × 5 languages), the evidence log carries `calendar:offset`, `statistics:<op>`, `unit_conversion:<step>`, `word_problem:<role>` events, and #1184's derivation record (`derivation::finalize_answer`) completes every route. The browser worker and the TypeScript twin answer the same probes (R1176-6). |
| R1176-6 | Worker parity: the unit-conversion, statistics, word-problem and calendar-offset computations answer identically in the browser worker and the TypeScript root (pull-request follow-up row: the three-roots half of R1176-5). | Implemented 2026-10-07: unit conversion, statistics, word problems and calendar offsets have browser-worker twins that reproduce the Rust handlers' exact-decimal arithmetic and derivation text, and `ts/` is regenerated from them; pinned by `rust/tests/web/issue-1176-unit-conversion-parity.test.mjs`, `issue-1176-statistics-parity.test.mjs` and `issue-1176-calendar-offset-parity.test.mjs`. |

## Issue #1177 Code Tasks Answered Formally

Issue [#1177](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1177) (E142,
part of the #1183 umbrella) gives the solver nine code-task families —
debugging, regular-expression synthesis, SQL synthesis, shell-command
composition, code explanation, code review, test generation, code
refactoring, and JSON/YAML format conversion — as structural derivations
from seed vocabulary, with every answer stating honestly that no code,
query, command, regex or generated test was executed. The probes, the
before/after evidence, and the honest boundaries live in
`docs/case-studies/issue-1177/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1177-1 | A "find the bug / debug this" request over a function is answered by deriving the defect structurally — a binary `+`/`-` applied at top level after a division shifts the quotient and contradicts what the function name promises — with the line quoted, both fixes shown (reorder, parenthesize), and the property grounded in a source. | Partial: `handle_code_debugging` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/code_debugging.rs` reads `def`/`fn`/`function` lines, resolves the name's promised property against the `function_intent` records in `data/seed/meanings-code-structure-explanations.lino` (each with a math source URL), and flags `sum(xs) / len(xs) - 1` as mean-minus-one with both candidate fixes; inline one-line returns are scanned too. The quotient-shift rule is the one implemented defect; other defect classes fall to the honest no-defect template. No code is executed and the answer says so. |
| R1177-2 | A regular-expression request ("five digits optionally followed by a hyphen and four digits") is composed from count, class, separator, optionality and anchor vocabulary, verified structurally, and never run against a string. | Partial: `handle_regex_synthesis` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/regex_synthesis.rs` composes from the seed word maps in `data/seed/code-task-cues.lino` (number words, classes, separators, optional markers, anchor exceptions) into anchored patterns — `^\d{5}(-\d{4})?$`, `\d{3,}` for "three or more" — and `verify_structurally` rejects dangling escapes and unbalanced repetition/parens/classes before answering. Unresolvable requests are refused by name. No match is executed and the answer says so. |
| R1177-3 | A SQL request ("select all users older than 30") is composed into a SELECT with table, columns, WHERE filters, aggregate, ORDER BY and LIMIT — each clause mapped back to the request words that produced it — and nothing is executed against a database. | Partial: `handle_sql_synthesis` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/sql_synthesis.rs` composes the statement from seed comparatives ("older than N" → `age > N`), generic column comparisons, named filters, aggregates, "sorted by X" and "top N" cues; the answer carries a request→emission mapping row per clause and states the verification is by construction. Only single SELECT statements; no joins, GROUP BY or subqueries. Identifying neither table nor cue refuses by name. |
| R1177-4 | A file-finding request ("find .log files larger than 10 MB under /var") is composed into a shell command with a cited manual page, and not executed. | Partial: `handle_shell_command_compose` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/shell_command_compose.rs` composes `find` with `-name` and `-size` clauses from the seed `file_context` and `size_unit` maps (MB/MiB → `M`, KB/KiB → `k`), cites the findutils manual, and marks the command Not executed. Only the find family; other shell verbs are refused by name rather than guessed. |
| R1177-5 | An "explain this code" request is answered line by line: each line matched against a construct table with a grounding URL, placeholders filled from the actual code, and an overall summary of what the function name promises. | Partial: `handle_code_explanation` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/code_explanation.rs` matches constructs (def, return, division, loops, builtins, conditionals, promise chains) from `data/seed/meanings-code-structure-explanations.lino`, each with sentence template and source, and closes with the name-promise summary. Unknown lines are skipped, not guessed; no code is executed and the answer says so. |
| R1177-6 | A "review this code" request reports only rule findings the code actually matches, each with severity, the quoted line, advice, and an upstream source URL — and no lint tool is run. | Partial: `handle_code_review` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/code_review.rs` applies the five seed rules in `data/seed/code-review-rules.lino` — bare `except:`, mutable default argument, `== None` instead of `is None`, `+=` string building in a loop (Python), loose `==` coercion (JavaScript) — each citing docs.python.org, PEP 8 or MDN. Language is detected from markers; a clean review says no match was found. No linter is executed and the answer says so. |
| R1177-7 | A "write tests for `f(x)`" request emits a runnable-looking pytest suite for a recognized problem shape, with expected values the shape's table states — and the suite is never executed. | Partial: `handle_test_generation` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/test_generation.rs` matches the function under test to the seed `test_cases` shapes (palindrome, average, max; trigger words are seed data), emits parametrized cases from the stated expectations (`RaceCar` → true, `never odd or even` → true, `[2, 4, 6]` → 4), and adds a `normalize()` helper when case-insensitivity/space/punctuation cues are present. Unknown shapes get a smoke skeleton and the derivation says the shape was not recognized. NOT executed, and the answer says so. |
| R1177-8 | A refactoring request performs the one implemented structural transformation — a JavaScript promise chain becomes an `async function` with `await`, handler bodies preserved verbatim — and refuses anything else by name. | Partial: `handle_code_refactoring` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/code_refactoring.rs` parses `.then`/`.catch` chains (arrow and `function` handlers), renders each `.then` as `const <param> = await <previous>;` in order with the catch clause preserved, and states the equivalence check is structural. Promise chains are the one transformation; other refactoring targets are refused by name. No code is executed and the answer says so. |
| R1177-9 | A JSON↔YAML conversion request converts the document, round-trips the result through the same subset parser, and compares against the input value; anything outside the subset is refused with a named reason. | Partial: `handle_format_conversion` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/format_conversion.rs` renders a JSON `Value` to block-style YAML and parses YAML back with a subset parser (mappings, sequences, scalars); the round-trip value equality check gates the answer, and bad JSON, a failed round trip or non-subset YAML each refuse through their own seed reason template. The subset excludes anchors, multi-line literals and flow style. No file or network I/O. |
| R1177-10 | All nine families are pure functions of seed data — cues, word maps, rule tables and answer prose live in `data/seed/` — refuse unrelated prompts, and are covered by automated tests at handler and engine level. | Implemented: recognition cues and word maps are in `data/seed/code-task-cues.lino`, review rules in `data/seed/code-review-rules.lino`, response templates in `data/seed/multilingual-responses.lino`, and every new intent key, scope, role and package token is defined in `data/seed/meanings-code-task-templates.lino`. `rust/tests/unit/issue_1177_code_task_handlers.rs` pins all nine probes at handler and engine level (the dispatch rows are wired in `rust/src/solver_dispatch.rs`), plus the refusal of unrelated prompts. All nine have browser-worker twins (`rust/tests/web/issue-1177-code-tasks-parity.test.mjs`, `issue-1177-code-synthesis-parity.test.mjs`, `issue-1177-format-conversion-parity.test.mjs`, `issue-1177-shell-compose-parity.test.mjs`), and `ts/` is regenerated from them. |
| R1177-11 | None of the nine sub-classes' answers ever recite a fetched Rosetta Code example verbatim (`rust/src/coding/rosetta_request.rs`'s `render_example` path is for the "example" intent only, not for explanation/debugging/review/etc.); the no-memorization gate (`rust/tests/unit/coding_discovery/no_memorization.rs`) is extended to scan the new handlers' output surfaces the same way it scans `coding-discovery-runtime.lino`. | Open follow-up (issue R11): the nine handlers compose every answer from seed templates and refuse rather than guess — none reads `rosetta_request.rs` — but the gate's scan is not yet extended to their output surfaces; the existing `no_memorization.rs` suite still passes unchanged over its current scan set. |
| R1177-12 | HumanEval and MBPP are re-measured on their full upstream slices after the change and the resulting pass counts are recorded, whatever they are, in `data/benchmarks/external-results.lino` (consumed by `docs/status.md`'s "Latest external benchmark rows" table). | Open follow-up (issue R12): not re-measured for this change; `data/benchmarks/external-results.lino` still carries the pre-change rows. The nine handlers are additive dispatch entries that no existing benchmark prompt routes to, but the issue's re-measurement requirement stands unmet and is recorded here as open. |

## Issue #1181 Standalone CLI Binaries and Consistent Boolean Env Switches

Issue [#1181](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1181) (E146,
part of the #1183 umbrella) has two halves: people cannot *run* the released
CLI at all (the release ships desktop apps and a VSIX but no standalone
`formal-ai` binary — the only channels are a full `cargo install` source build
or a 24.3 GB container image, #1153), and the one env switch that gates CLI
output rejects the conventional `1`/`0` spellings (`FORMAL_AI_SILENT=1
formal-ai chat …` fails with `invalid value '1' for '--silent' [possible
values: true, false]`). The evidence, the design, and the per-file change list
live in `docs/case-studies/issue-1181/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1181-1 | `.github/workflows/desktop-release.yml` gains a `cli` job that builds `formal-ai` for `x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`, `aarch64-unknown-linux-musl`, `x86_64-apple-darwin`, `aarch64-apple-darwin`, `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` and uploads one archive per target to the same GitHub Release the `build`/`vscode` jobs publish to. | Delivered as workflow: the `cli` job in `.github/workflows/desktop-release.yml` (five-leg matrix mirroring the `build` job's needs/concurrency/if/permissions/checkout/sccache conventions, `taiki-e/setup-cross-toolchain-action@v1` for the musl legs because the dependency graph compiles C code). Observable on the next tagged release, whose asset list must show the five `formal-ai-cli-*` archives; until then it is code-reviewed, not executed. |
| R1181-2 | Each archive is named `formal-ai-cli-<target-triple>.tar.gz` (`.zip` for the Windows target), contains the `formal-ai` binary plus `LICENSE` and `README.md` under a top-level `formal-ai-cli-<triple>/` directory, and is reproducible from `cargo build --release --target <triple> --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --bin formal-ai --locked`. | Delivered as workflow: the "Package the CLI archive" and "Smoke test CLI archive" steps build with the exact pinned-lock command, package the staging directory, then extract the archive on the leg's own runner and run `./formal-ai --version` plus non-emptiness checks on `LICENSE`/`README.md`. |
| R1181-3 | The `finalize` job's consolidated `SHA256SUMS.txt` and `BUILD-PROVENANCE.txt` cover the five CLI archives alongside the existing desktop/VSIX assets, in the same files, with the same "INCOMPLETE" honesty reporting for partial matrices. | Delivered as workflow: `cli` joins `finalize`'s `needs`; each leg uploads a `SHA256SUMS-cli-<label>.partial` fragment (the `cli-` label prefix prevents collision with the desktop legs' identically-shaped labels in the merged `fragments/` directory); the `builder_of` map and label loop in `finalize` gain the five `cli-*` labels mapped to their runners. |
| R1181-4 | `rust/Cargo.toml` gains a `[package.metadata.binstall]` table so `cargo binstall formal-ai` resolves one of the R2 archives without a source build. | Delivered: `[package.metadata.binstall]` (`pkg-url` …/`formal-ai-cli-{ target }.tar.gz`, `pkg-fmt "tgz"`, `bin-dir "formal-ai-cli-{ target }/{ bin }{ binary-ext }"`) with a `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` override to the `.zip`; the URL is written out literally because the archive name ends `.tar.gz`, not binstall's default `{ archive-suffix }` (`.tgz`). Executed only when the first release carrying the assets exists. |
| R1181-5 | `scripts/install.sh`'s `install_cli()` and `install.ps1`'s equivalent download and verify the matching `formal-ai-cli-<target>` archive first, falling back to `cargo install formal-ai` only when no matching archive exists for the host's OS/arch (e.g. windows-arm64, which R1 does not build). | Delivered: `install_cli_prebuilt`/`Install-CliPrebuilt` resolve the host triple, fetch the archive, verify it against the release's `SHA256SUMS.txt` through the existing `verify_checksum`/`Test-Checksum` helpers, run the installed binary's `--version`, and only then report success; any unavailable/failed prebuilt path falls back to the unchanged `cargo install` body. A checksum mismatch still aborts (it never falls back silently). `install.ps1` could not be machine-parsed on this macOS workstation (no PowerShell); it follows the file's existing cmdlet idioms and is review-verified. |
| R1181-6 | A single boolean-env parser accepts `1/0/true/false/yes/no/on/off` case-insensitively (surrounding whitespace tolerated; anything else is unrecognised, never silently coerced), is the `value_parser` for every clap arg with `env = "FORMAL_AI_*"` on a `bool` field, and is used by every ad-hoc `std::env::var("FORMAL_AI_*")` boolean read in `rust/src`. | Delivered and tested: `rust/src/cli_env.rs` (`parse_bool_env`, `bool_env_value_parser`, `flag_enabled`, `flag_disabled`) wired into `rust/src/main.rs`'s `--silent` (the only clap bool arg with an `env` attribute in the crate) and into every ad-hoc boolean read — the full converted-site list is in `docs/case-studies/issue-1181/README.md`. `solver_helpers::env_bool`/`env_bool_with_extra_truthy` now delegate to the same table so there is one spelling vocabulary crate-wide. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1181_boolean_env_parser.rs`. The one intentional exception: `FORMAL_AI_FULL_TRUST` (`rust/src/bounded_autonomy.rs`) keeps its exact-`"1"` sentinel because it is a security opt-in, not a UX switch. `rust/src/translation/pipeline.rs`'s `FORMAL_AI_TRANSLATION_DEBUG` read is deferred to the issue-#1174 change that owns that file. |
| R1181-7 | `FORMAL_AI_SILENT=1 formal-ai chat --prompt …` (and `=true`, `=yes`, `=on`, case-insensitive, and their false-y counterparts) no longer errors, and the non-clap `verbose_enabled()` read of the same variable honours the same spellings. | Delivered and tested: the `value_parser = formal_ai::cli_env::bool_env_value_parser` attribute on `--silent` (the `SetTrue` action is preserved, so a bare `--silent` flag still works), and `dialog_log::verbose_enabled()`'s second read goes through `!flag_enabled("FORMAL_AI_SILENT")`. Pinned by `silent_switch_now_accepts_one_as_the_issue_reported` and `bool_env_value_parser_maps_spellings_to_clap_results` in the same test file, which assert the exact truth table for the reported failing value. |
